title: The 14th Round of the Matsue Tamatsukuri Linked Verse Contest
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro, Ran) and case-specific procedural-only police (Hirose, Yasugi, Tsubaki) omitted by convention -- none of them are suspects/victims/witnesses with personal stakes in the plot; Tsubaki's shoe-fingerprint finding is represented as an attribute of the shoe object instead. The old wiki-derived case file (cases/ep255-256_...json) had the right culprit (Shiina) but reduced the whole case to 2 generic clue nodes and 3 event nodes, collapsing distinct facts (stolen phone, hidden camera, torn notebook page, planted eye drops, manipulated lots, the shoe-hook dying message, the acrostic confession, the recited-stolen-verse trap) into two vague clue blobs, and gave only a placeholder 'unspecified' motive. The transcript supports a much richer graph: Shiina rigged the location lots the night before so Ushikubo would draw the isolated Matsue Castle promenade and he himself would draw the distant Teien Art Museum for an easy alibi; he stole Ushikubo's spare phone and used it to lure Yagisawa (the framed red herring, who owed Ushikubo money) to Jozan Inari Shrine; he set up a hidden camera near the Teien Art Museum pond to fake continuous presence there; he killed Ushikubo with blunt trauma, planted Yagisawa's lost eye drops by the body, dumped the bloody raincoat and weapon in the Gessho-ji pond, tore the page with a plagiarized verse out of Ushikubo's notebook, and was caught only when Kogoro maneuvered him into reciting that exact stolen verse aloud during the contest and Officer Tsubaki matched Ushikubo's bloody dying fingerprint to the hook on Shiina's own shoe (the true meaning of the dying message, previously misread as pointing at bamboo/the samurai mansion). Mizuki Kawaguchi is a suspect who is also functionally a witness/red herring: out of unrequited love for Yagisawa she deviated from her assigned alibi location, actually reached the crime scene shortly after the murder, then fabricated a cover verse for an alibi location whose described autumn colors are not visible from where she claimed to be sitting -- exposed by Conan as a physical contradiction, not evidence of murder. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Ushikubo's dying gesture was assumed to point at nearby bamboo, or across the canal toward the samurai mansions -- but re-examined, it actually encoded the number "1" (the position of the hokku, the linked verse's first line, punning on "hook") and matches a bloody fingerprint recovered from the hook on Shiina's own shoe, the very shoe admired earlier at the hotel.

Mizuki's claimed alibi verse describes autumn colors she says she saw while composing at the Shiomi Nawate rest area, but thick shrubs actually block any view of autumn colors from that spot -- proving she was somewhere else (in fact, at the crime scene) when she says she wrote it.
